description: THE AGENT-SIDE ADOPTION SAFETY GATE (Wave 6). The conversation experiment world's judge nets its score (flagged_changed - regressions), so a variant that fixes the flagged turn but breaks one other previously-working turn can still judge 'supported' (+2-1=+1) and reach mark_adopt_ready. This seed closes that hole AS GRAPH DATA the agent can inspect and repair: the dispatched child already reports `regressions` in result.json, the dispatch ingest (domains/experiment_dispatch.py::_ingest_result) mechanically carries it onto the Experiment node, and the rule below VETOES adoption of any Experiment whose own child reported regressions > 0 -- it sets `adopt_denied` (which perform_adoptions honours unconditionally: a denied Experiment is never folded back) plus an honest `adopt_denied_reason` the self_improvement_status reader surfaces over NL ('what are you working on?'). Chosen over a stricter mark_adopt_ready where-clause deliberately: the authored mark_adopt_ready_* bodies stay byte-identical (graph-meta oracle parity with seeds/composer_experiment_graph.json's wants_experiment_adopt_rule is preserved untouched), the veto applies uniformly to every experiment family that reports regressions (today: conversation replay), and an ARC child reports no `regressions` key at all, so the attr is never written there and this rule can never bind an ARC experiment. The veto fires in the same run_rules fixpoint as the judge/mark_adopt_ready rules (the regressions attr is written at ingest, before that tick), so perform_adoptions -- host I/O that only runs between ticks -- always sees the denial before it could adopt. || v1.1.0 (2026-10-10): adopt_denied_on_overridden_verdict -- an adopt-ready Experiment whose outcome a family judge has since overridden away from 'supported' is vetoed (measured: tranche 23 smoke run, adopted=True with outcome='refuted'; scripts/gen_adoption_overridden_verdict_veto.py). || v1.2.0 (2026-10-10, plan P1 judge v2): adopt_denied_on_quality_drop vetoes adoption when the child's ReplyQuality report shows any turn's quality fell or the mean fell (scripts/gen_adoption_quality_veto.py).

microtheory.name: adoption_safety
microtheory.description: a supported-but-regressing variant is never adopted: regressions == 0 is a hard adopt-readiness requirement, held as an inspectable seed rule.

rules.name: adopt_denied_on_regression
effects: the dispatched child reported regressions > 0: a variant that breaks a previously-working turn is never adopted, even when its net score judges supported

rules.name: adopt_denied_on_overridden_verdict
rules.comment: adoption_safety v1.1.0: an adopt-ready Experiment whose final outcome is no longer 'supported' (a family judge overrode the generic verdict) is never adopted.
effects: the experiment was marked adopt-ready on a provisional 'supported' verdict that a later judge overrode: a change the agent's own final verdict does not support is never adopted

rules.name: adopt_denied_on_quality_drop
rules.comment: Judge v2 (plan P1): a variant that lowers any replayed turn's reply quality, or the mean, is never adopted.
effects: judge v2: the dispatched child reported a reply-quality drop (quality_drops > 0 or quality_delta < 0): a variant that makes a reply worse is never adopted
